name: Siargao
tagline: The surfing capital of the Philippines, a teardrop of palm groves, rock pools and lagoons around the famous Cloud 9 break.
highlight: Watching surfers ride the tubing waves of Cloud 9 from the boardwalk at sunrise.
shortDescription: A laid-back island with the Cloud 9 surf break, the Sugba and Magpupungko lagoons and rock pools, Naked Island, Sohoton Cove and a growing café and yoga scene.
metaDescription: A Siargao travel guide: Cloud 9 surfing, Magpupungko rock pools, Sugba Lagoon, Naked, Daku and Guyam islands, Sohoton Cove, general Luna town, where to stay, how to get there and a four-day plan.

image.alt: The Cloud 9 boardwalk and surf break on Siargao Island

intro: Siargao is a teardrop-shaped island off the north-east coast of Mindanao, and the surfing capital of the Philippines. Its main break, Cloud 9, a fast, hollow reef wave breaking just off General Luna, has hosted international surfing competitions since the 1990s, and the island now supports a laid-back scene of surf schools, cafés, yoga studios and hostels. It was hit hard by Typhoon Rai in December 2021, and has since rebuilt.

Surfing is best from August to November, when swells are biggest, but Siargao is an attractive island year-round. Coconut palm forests cover much of it, and inland there are mangrove-lined lagoons. Off the coast near General Luna, three islands, Naked Island, Daku Island and Guyam Island, form the classic island-hopping trip. In the north-east, the Magpupungko rock pools appear at low tide, and Sugba Lagoon offers clear green water for swimming.

Beginners can learn to surf on gentler waves, and non-surfers can enjoy scooter rides through palm groves, sunsets and beach clubs. The town of General Luna is the base, and the island is reached by a short flight from Cebu or Manila. The vibe is relaxed and increasingly cosmopolitan, and it is calmer than Boracay.
